reviews.title: Here's a 'probpem', made by the promoters of Asthis App...
reviews.text:
This app's so-so. It's okay if you're really not familiar with how an (I)phone stores data.

I've found that many people of various ages share this lack of understanding.

Why do I say this?

Because of the idiotic TV ads which keep popping up with all the subtlety of web-based marketing.

At what age do these micro-brains think 'old' begins?

When I was under ten, that was a pretty extensive range.

Same if I were a teenager, etc.

Here's the thing: it's not the age nor the age range which causes the mistakes—specifically, misunderstandings about how data accumulates and should be handled. It's not fully understanding HOW the data's managed by the device.

That could be due to many reasons, including a lack of education. But, you see, even saying that, I'm likely to upset some people by implying something about their education, which isn't politically correct—it’s just one of many possible reasons.

Do older people make the same mistake? Undoubtedly. 

But I don't know exactly what age range it includes, nor do I have comparative data from other groups or any predefined group, So, to imply this is something solely done by 'old people's is obnoxious, and it's incorrect.

I taught myself Mac computers in the days before Intel processors and the 'OS'; it was known as 'system' (in my case, '7', and it wasn't called 'System', just plain 'system'). Since then, I've not only kept up but have stayed ahead.
